rows.citation: Nguyen J et al. 2024, Anticancer Research
rows.n: narrative review (no human efficacy studies to pool)
rows.finding: Review of oral fenbendazole for cancer concludes all anticancer evidence is preclinical (in vitro / animal) and explicitly states clinical trials are still needed to assess anticancer effect, dose and safety in humans — no human efficacy demonstrated.
rows.integrity_note: Verified PMID:39197912, DOI 10.21873/anticanres.17197; abstract confirms preclinical-only and explicit call for trials. Design note: this is a narrative review; mapped to nearest allowed vocabulary term 'systematic review'.

rows.citation: Yamaguchi T et al. 2021, Case Reports in Oncology
rows.finding: First human report of self-administered fenbendazole for cancer: patient developed severe drug-induced liver injury and had NO tumor shrinkage — anticancer claim not supported, net harm observed.
rows.integrity_note: Verified PMID:34248555, DOI 10.1159/000516276; abstract confirms DILI and explicitly 'she did not experience tumor shrinkage'.

rows.citation: Skaara TR et al. 2025, Tidsskrift for den Norske Laegeforening
rows.finding: Cancer patient taking 2 g/day fenbendazole as alternative therapy developed cholestasis with biopsy-confirmed lobular/portal liver inflammation; framed as unproven alternative treatment causing toxicity, no efficacy benefit.
rows.integrity_note: Verified PMID:41097960, DOI 10.4045/tidsskr.25.0229; Norwegian-language case report, abstract confirms 2 g/day fenbendazole, cholestasis and biopsy-confirmed inflammation.

rows.finding: In vivo mouse study: therapeutic fenbendazole diet (150 ppm) did NOT alter tumor growth, invasion or metastasis and did not enhance radiation response — a direct in-vivo null for antitumor efficacy.
rows.integrity_note: Verified PMID:22776123 (PMC3314526); abstract confirms 'medicated diet did not alter tumor growth, invasion, or metastasis'. Mouse study — population_match false, correct.

rows.citation: Dogra N et al. 2018, Scientific Reports
rows.n: A549 human cell lines + nu/nu mouse xenografts
rows.finding: Fenbendazole acts as a moderate microtubule destabilizer, inhibits glucose uptake/GLUT-HKII, and slowed human tumor xenograft growth in nude mice fed the drug orally — supportive but strictly preclinical (cells + mice).
rows.integrity_note: Verified PMID:30093705, DOI 10.1038/s41598-018-30158-6; no retraction or expression-of-concern found on PubMed record or web search as of 2026-07.

rows.citation: Chang CS et al. 2023, Journal of Gynecologic Oncology
rows.n: ovarian cancer cell lines + PDX/xenograft mice
rows.finding: Plain oral fenbendazole showed NO tumor reduction in ovarian-cancer xenografts (poor solubility); only IV-administered PLGA-nanoparticle reformulation reduced tumor weight — highlighting that the oral route humans self-dose failed even in mice.
rows.integrity_note: Verified PMID:37170725, DOI 10.3802/jgo.2023.34.e58. Note: direction=+1 reflects net positive anticancer signal for reformulated FZ, but the abstract explicitly states oral FZ had 'no effect on tumor reduction' — supportive only for a non-human, non-oral formulation.

rows.citation: Park D et al. 2022, Korean Journal of Physiology & Pharmacology
rows.n: SNU-C5 colorectal cancer cell lines (in vitro)
rows.finding: Fenbendazole induced apoptosis and G2/M arrest in 5-FU-resistant colorectal cancer cells in vitro — mechanistic cell-culture support only, no in-vivo or human evidence.
rows.integrity_note: Verified PMID:36039738, DOI 10.4196/kjpp.2022.26.5.377; in vitro only, population_match false correct.

provenance: Gathered in-window from PubMed/ClinicalTrials.gov (public). PMIDs/NCTs/DOIs only; no Consensus output redistributed.

baseline.text: Fenbendazole is an animal deworming drug with no proven clinical evidence that it treats cancer in humans.
